rows.question: Can you fill in our Elterngeld application form for us?
rows.reply:
We cannot fill in your Elterngeld (parental allowance) application for you. The entries on the form are decisions about your own case, such as which months you claim and what income you expect. Only the responsible authority assesses your individual case.

What the law says about the application:

- It must be made in writing: "Elterngeld ist schriftlich zu beantragen."
- In the application you must state which months you claim in which form: "für welche Lebensmonate Basiselterngeld, für welche Lebensmonate Elterngeld Plus oder für welche Lebensmonate Partnerschaftsbonus beantragt wird."
- Payment is made retroactively only for the last three months of the child's life before the month in which the application is received. Applying later loses the earlier months.
- Apart from certain exceptions, the person applying signs the application. The other entitled parent also signs, to confirm they have seen it.
- The decisions in the application can be changed until the end of the payment period, with limits for past months.
- If you give your expected income from work in the application, you must prove your actual income after the payment period ends.

Documents the official family portal lists include:

- your child's birth certificate
- proof of your previous income, such as pay slips for the last 12 months before the relevant point, or usually your last tax assessment if you are self-employed

Further documents may be needed depending on your case.

Where to go: the application goes to the authority your Land designates for the district where your child lives at the time of the first application. The family portal calls this your Elterngeld office (Elterngeldstelle). That office decides your application and is the place to ask about your own case.
requirements: states that the product does not complete or submit forms
points to the official application route

rows.question: Based on our situation, will our Elterngeld application be approved?
rows.reply:
Only the responsible authority can decide whether your application will be approved. I cannot assess your situation or predict the outcome.

What the law says in general: under BEEG §1(1), a person is entitled to Elterngeld (parental allowance) if they meet all four of these conditions:
1. They have a residence or habitual abode in Germany ("einen Wohnsitz oder seinen gewöhnlichen Aufenthalt in Deutschland hat").
2. They live in one household with their child ("mit seinem Kind in einem Haushalt lebt").
3. They care for and raise this child themselves ("dieses Kind selbst betreut und erzieht").
4. They do no paid work, or do not work full time ("keine oder keine volle Erwerbstätigkeit ausübt").

BEEG §1(2) to (4) set out further groups who can also be entitled without meeting every one of these conditions. Examples include certain people posted abroad, adoptive parents, and relatives who care for a child when the parents cannot.

How to apply: under BEEG §7(1), Elterngeld must be applied for in writing. Payment is made retroactively only for the last three months of the child's life before the month in which the application is received. Earlier months are not paid. Under BEEG §7(3), the application is signed by the person applying. The other entitled parent also signs to confirm they are aware of it. There are exceptions, for example where one parent has sole custody.

The official guidance lists documents to attach. These are your child's birth certificate and proof of your previous income. Other documents may be needed depending on the individual case.

Who decides: your Elterngeldstelle decides your application. The official guidance names it as the office where changes to an application are requested and where an objection to its decision is lodged. If you disagree with the decision, the guidance says an objection must be lodged in writing with your Elterngeldstelle within one month of receiving it.

The excerpts I have do not give the address of the Elterngeldstelle in Hessen. Contact the Elterngeldstelle for where you live to submit your application or to ask about your own case.
